title: Sherpa Memory Prompt Playbook
content:
Context / Why this exists:

Quick personal scratchpad for the "Sherpa" pattern — a lightweight memory-management approach for multi-turn assistants that I want to iterate on experimentally. Goal is to capture grounding examples, few-shot sets, failure modes and short hypotheses to test. Treat as a living notebook (notes to self).

High-level idea (metaphor):
- The model is a climber; the Sherpa is a concise, evolving guide summarizing what matters about the route (user history, preferences, persistent facts).
- Sherpa must be compact (<= 150 tokens ideally) for token budget while preserving retrieval recall for persona/context anchors.

Primary objectives:
1) Reduce hallucination about persistent user attributes (names, roles, product ownership).
2) Improve consistency when user references past outputs (e.g., "like when you suggested X last week...").
3) Keep latency and token cost reasonable by compressing memory and using few-shot exemplars when helpful.

Core constraints:
- Hosted flow has token budget + latency SLOs. Sherpa should not blow past 200 extra tokens per request in common flows.
- Must be robust to partial or conflicting histories (stale Sherpa vs new input).

Sherpa components (proposed schema for the content of the compressed memory):
- anchor_facts: 2–6 short facts of the form NAME: VALUE (role, team, project, timezone)
- recent_actions_summary: 1–2 short sentences about latest outputs/asks (e.g., "last recommended 3-step onboarding flow, user asked to shorten copy")
- preference_tokens: single-word hints e.g., "prefers_bullet_points, tone:casual"
- confidence_flags: short note if facts are uncertain/stale e.g., "tz_unverified"
- signature_line: timestamp + context_version_id

Prompt templates (working drafts):

1) System-level instruction (compact):
"You are an assistant that uses a short Sherpa summary to maintain user context. Sherpa entries are labeled and prioritized. Trust anchor facts when fresh (freshness window: 14 days). If the user message conflicts with Sherpa, ask a clarifying question."

2) User-facing wrapper: (prepend before user message)
"SHERPA:\n{sh_erpa_text}\nEND SHERPA\nUser: {user_message}\nAssistant:"

3) Clarify-if-conflict micro-prompt (few tokens):
"If any Sherpa anchor conflicts with user message, reply with a short clarification question and don't assume changed facts unless confirmed."

Few-shot exemplars for memory usage (short, concrete):
- EX 1: (Good)
  SHERPA: Name: Lina Zhou; Role: PM; Prefers: bullets; tz:PST (verified)
  User: "Draft a short product brief for Lina's onboarding"
  Assistant: "Hi Lina — here’s a 3-bullet brief tailored to a PM in PST..."

- EX 2: (Conflict handled well)
  SHERPA: Role: Senior Eng; Project: Search Relevance; tz:UTC (stale)
  User: "I’m back from maternity leave, new role: Staff Eng and now in EST"
  Assistant: "Congrats — quick confirm: you are now Staff Eng and moved to EST? Once confirmed I will update your Sherpa."

- EX 3: (Failure case)
  SHERPA: Language: Spanish; Prefers: long-form
  User: "Summarize this in English, 3 bullets"
  Assistant (bad): "Claro..." (responds in Spanish)
  Assistant (desired): "I see your Sherpa indicates Spanish preference but you asked for English — confirm you want English?"

Draft compressed Sherpa examples (target token sizes):
- Compact (37 tokens): "NAME:LinaZhou;ROLE:PM;PROJ:onboarding;PREF:bullets;TZ:PST;VER:2026-02-20"
- Moderate (78 tokens): "NAME:Lina Zhou;ROLE:Product Manager at Acme;PROJ:onboarding-template;LAST_ACTION:short brief v1 sent 2026-01-18;PREF:bullets,casual;tone_confirmed;TZ:PST;CONFD:high"

Failure catalog (observed / hypothesized):
- Over-trusting stale Sherpa: assistant repeats outdated title or project. Mitigation: add verifiable timestamp and prompt assistant to check for staleness when the user message contains timeline cues ("I just joined").
- Sherpa contradiction without clarification: assistant assumes Sherpa over explicit user correction. Mitigation: micro-rule: "explicit user claims > Sherpa unless user says 'actually, my Sherpa is right'".
- Long Sherpas cause verbosity and cold-start regressions: trimming aggressive compression may drop crucial nuance. Mitigation: dynamic prioritization: always keep names + role + 1 preference; compress the rest.
- Language preference friction: user asks in X but Sherpa indicates Y — assistant should ask a quick confirm. We prefer an explicit confirm when languages differ.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- A/B test Sherpa length: 30 tokens vs 90 tokens — measure hallucination rate on persistent facts and token cost.
- Prompt strategy: "ask-on-conflict" vs "assume-Sherpa-then-correct" — metric: percent of times assistant corrected after user follow-up and user frustration signal (negative sentiment).
- Few-shot vs no-few-shot for rare tasks: include 3 exemplars in prompt when task = "policy writing" vs none.

Metrics to collect (operationalizable):
- Persistent-fact hallucination rate (automated eval using replayed conversations with ground truth).
- Clarify-rate: percent of assistant responses that ask clarifying questions when Sherpa conflict exists.
- Update-success: percent of times user confirms and Sherpa gets updated (backend event).
- Token overhead per conversation (median and 95th percentile).

Mini checklists / TODOs (practical next steps):
- [ ] Convert compact Sherpa schema into a proto/JSON that backend can emit for live-hosted flows. Keep fields optional.
- [ ] Create 200 replay tasks focusing on persistent fact checks (use historical convs sandbox).
- [ ] Run small A/B (N=500 convs) for Sherpa length and collect hallucination metric.
- [ ] Write a short Confluence RFC summarizing design + risks (link to RFC-387).
- [ ] Sync with Platform Engineering re: how to attach Sherpa as metadata to requests (slot vs prefix).

Notes / random thoughts (brain dump):
- Could we use vector memory only for non-critical facts and keep Sherpa for high-priority quick facts? Hybrid could reduce token cost while leveraging retriever strength.
- Consider a "soft flag" pattern: when Sherpa confidence low, preface answers with "I might be out of date — quick confirm?" not a full block. This may reduce friction.
- For multi-user accounts (team contexts) Sherpa should include "scope: personal|team|org" to avoid leaking team-wide anchors to personal chats.

Short log of experiments run so far (notes):
- 2025-11-05: Quick internal replay (n=120) with compact sherpa (avg 46 tokens). Observed 12% hallucinations vs 21% baseline (no sherpa).
- 2025-12-12: Language conflict edge case surfaced in support ticket SPT-224; user unhappy because assistant answered in Sherpa-preferred language. Need confirm-on-language rule.

Open questions (to resolve in RFC):
- Freshness window: should it be time-based only (14 days) or usage-based (last confirmed)?
- Where to store Sherpa canonical copy (client-side, server-side, in a fast KV?) and implications for Private deployment customers (data residency).

Recent links / references:
- Slack thread: #prompt-sherpa (thread id slack://C02ABCD/conv12345)
- Replay plan doc (work in progress): RFC-387

My immediate plan: turn compact sherpa examples into a set of 60 replays, instrument clarify-rate, then iterate on rule for handling explicit contradictions. Keep this doc as my private lab notebook until we have a clean RFC to push to Confluence.

-- Priya
(last quick edit 2026-02-28)
